changes.before: Implement timeoutOutcome(clientTimedOut,receipt). Match the worked contract and the changed-input checks without modifying the supplied input values.
changes.after: A timeout means the browser stopped waiting. The server may still have completed the request.

before: A client timeout means the client stopped waiting. It does not prove whether a remote write completed before or after that point.
This exercise is a small pure JavaScript model. Its inputs are supplied directly; it does not receive live HTTP requests, operate a database, or deploy a service.
The first branch accepts an actual successful operation receipt in this model. Without one, a timeout gives an unknown outcome. Reconcile that outcome before repeating a non-idempotent action.

Read the function call timeoutOutcome(true, null) from the inside out: the arguments supply the inputs, timeoutOutcome runs the body once, and return sends its result back to the caller. console.log displays that result; it does not change it.
The client times out after sending a creation request. Is it safe to claim nothing was created? The server may have completed the write while the response was lost or delayed.
after: A timeout happens when a caller stops waiting for a reply. It does not undo work on the server or prove that the work failed.
A receipt is confirmation that the operation succeeded. This exercise assumes any supplied receipt is already checked and really confirms success.
Check the receipt first. If it exists, return "confirmed". Without a receipt, return "unknown" after a timeout or "waiting" while the caller is still waiting.
Before repeating a request that creates data, find out whether the original succeeded or use a design that prevents duplicates. A missing reply alone is not enough evidence.
Try a valid receipt after a timeout. The helper should return "confirmed": the receipt settles the result even though the reply arrived late.

No, the outcome may be unknown

after.question: A caller times out after asking the server to create a note. Does that prove no note was created?
choices: Yes. A timeout undoes all server work.
No. The outcome may be unknown.
Yes, if no response body arrived.
after.explanation: The server may have created the note while the reply was delayed or lost.

headings: Waiting can end before the work

project.title: Do not infer failure from a client timeout
project.task: Complete timeoutOutcome(clientTimedOut,receipt). A supplied success receipt means "confirmed". Otherwise return "unknown" after a timeout or "waiting" before one.
project.done_when: The checks pass with and without a receipt, including a receipt after a timeout. Explain why a timeout does not prove the server did nothing.
